name: BAT54
description: Planar small-signal Schottky in SOT-23 with a guard ring, 30V / 200mA, low drop and ~5ns recovery. Signal detection/clamping, voltage clamping, steering/OR-ing, and small DC/DC catch diodes. The plain BAT54 is a single diode; the A/C/S suffixes are dual-diode variants differing only in internal interconnection.

pins.name: A
pins.description: single BAT54: anode. A=K1, C=A1, S=A1 on the dual variants (see gotchas)

pins.name: NC
pins.description: single BAT54: no connection. A=K2, C=A2, S=K2 on the dual variants

pins.name: K
pins.description: single BAT54: cathode. A=common anode, C=common cathode, S=series midpoint

typical_application: Signal-level rectification/detection, clamping, and steering; the A/C/S variants pack two diodes in one SOT-23 for clamp networks and OR-ing.
gotchas: the suffix changes the internal topology, not just packaging: BAT54=single (pin2 NC), BAT54A=common anode pair, BAT54C=common cathode pair, BAT54S=two in series with midpoint on pin3 - swapping suffixes silently breaks the circuit (verify the marking code)
plain BAT54 single has NO connection on pin 2; do not route a net through it
Schottky reverse leakage (up to 2uA at 25V, rising with temperature) is far higher than a silicon 1N4148; matters on high-impedance / sample-and-hold nodes
only 30V reverse and 200mA; it is a small-signal part, not a power rectifier
